conventions.base64: standard alphabet (A-Z a-z 0-9 + /) with '=' padding on output; decoders accept standard and URL-safe alphabets, padded or not, and ignore \n \r space \t
conventions.byte_order: all multi-byte integers inside binary layouts are big-endian (len16be)
conventions.hex: lowercase on output; decoders accept either case
conventions.integers: Unix seconds as JSON integers; decimal ASCII inside signing strings
conventions.json: key order is never significant; the reference emits keys sorted alphabetically
conventions.strings: UTF-8; '\n' inside a signing string is the single byte 0x0a; no trailing newline

meta.purpose: Known-answer vectors so that a re-implementation of the R2R relay in another language can prove byte-exact compatibility with the reference C++ relay's cryptography, canonical strings and encodings before it ever talks to the network.
meta.regenerate: cmake -S . -B build -DR2R_BUILD_VECTORS=ON && cmake --build build --target r2r-vectors && ./build/r2r-vectors > docs/protocol-vectors.json
meta.stability: Every value is a function of the fixed inputs in the source. Blobs from randomised primitives (sealed boxes) were generated once and embedded as constants; the generator opens them with the public API on every run, and two runs print identical documents.
meta.whitepaper: protocol/R2R-WHITEPAPER.md sections 3 (conventions), 4 (identities), 10 (onion) and Appendix A. Values marked whitepaper_ref reproduce Appendix A and are asserted by the generator.

multi_recipient_layer.aad: the header: 0x02 || n || all n slots (2 + 93n bytes)
multi_recipient_layer.cipher: AES-256-GCM under K with a fresh 12-byte nonce

negative.case: n set to 1 and slot 2 removed

embedded.plaintext: r2r multi-recipient layer vector: relay A or relay B may open this

multi_recipient_layer.layout: 0x02 || n(1) || n x slot(93) || nonce(12) || ciphertext || tag(16); slot_i = seal(candidate_i.x25519_pub, K) where K is a fresh 32-byte layer key (61 + 32 = 93 bytes); 1 <= n <= 3; minimum total 123 bytes
multi_recipient_layer.note: nothing says which slot belongs to which relay; an opener tries every slot in order and uses the first that unseals to exactly 32 bytes
multi_recipient_layer.verify: For each slot i, try unseal(slot_i) with your x25519 key; a 32-byte result is the layer key K; then AES-256-GCM-decrypt(K, nonce, ciphertext||tag, aad = header) and compare 'plaintext'. relay_c must fail on every slot; swapped slots must fail the tag for everyone.

whitepaper_a4b.note: sealed by the reference wallet (JavaScript) with fixed K, nonces and ephemeral keys listed in the white paper; both candidates open it with libr2r_core

node_identity.verify: node_id = lowercase_hex(SHA-256('r2r-node-v1' || ed25519_pub))[0..32] (first 16 bytes); x25519_priv = HKDF-SHA256(ikm = seed, salt = empty, info = 'r2r-x25519-v1', L = 32); x25519_pub = X25519(x25519_priv, basepoint 9) with RFC 7748 clamping.

x25519_hkdf.note: the x25519 private key is NOT the ed25519 key converted; it is an independent HKDF output of the same seed

onion.build_order: seal the terminal plaintext to the last position; then for each earlier position, from last to first: plaintext = routing header naming the NEXT position's candidates || the layer just built, sealed to this position's candidates
onion.client_frame: {"t":"onion","blob":"<base64 outer layer>"} sent with NO hello; success is silent
onion.layer: each layer is a multi-recipient sealed box (see multi_recipient_layer) sealed to the 1..3 candidates of one route position; the outermost layer is what the client sends

hop_a.forwards_to: the first 'next' candidate with a live link, else dialled in order; itself is skipped
the first 'next' candidate with a live link, else dialled in order; itself is skipped

route_a_then_b_or_c.note: relay_c is a standby terminal: it opens the same layer and, because 'home' names relay_b, forwards the payload there as an ordinary send; relay_b stores it

onion.routing_plaintext: 0x01 || n(1) || n x ( len8 || "host:port" ) || inner layer bytes; addresses are the sender's text and are canonicalised by the relay with parse_address(default port 8787); the inner layer must be >= 123 bytes
onion.terminal_plaintext: 0x02 || len16be(2) || meta JSON (UTF-8) || body; meta = {"to":"<fp>[@<home relay>]","id":"<uuid4>","hint"?:"<=128 chars"}; body is 1..max_payload bytes of end-to-end ciphertext; the reference builder emits meta keys in alphabetical order (hint, id, to) but any order parses
onion.verify: Open 'blob' with relay_a (multi-recipient layer), parse the routing plaintext, forward 'inner_blob' to a 'next' candidate, open it there and parse the terminal record; compare every field. A port that builds routes should produce blobs that these relays peel to the same plaintexts (the blobs themselves differ because sealing is randomised).

kdf.aad: 0x01 || eph_pub || recipient_x25519_pub (65 bytes): the version byte and both public keys
kdf.cipher: AES-256-GCM, 12-byte nonce, 16-byte tag appended to the ciphertext
kdf.hkdf: HKDF-SHA256(ikm = shared, salt = eph_pub || recipient_x25519_pub (64 bytes), info = "r2r-seal-v1", L = 32)
kdf.note: the recipient's own public key is bound into both the HKDF salt and the AAD, so a blob sealed to one relay cannot be opened by, or re-targeted to, another
kdf.shared: X25519(eph_priv, recipient_x25519_pub); an all-zero result MUST be rejected

sealed_box.layout: version(1)=0x01 || eph_pub(32) || nonce(12) || ciphertext || tag(16); overhead 61 bytes

library_generated.generated_by: crypto::seal(relay_a.x_pub, plaintext) with a random ephemeral key and nonce, run once
library_generated.plaintext: r2r sealed-box vector: plaintext for relay A

sealed_box.verify: Open 'blob' with relay_a's x25519 private key following 'layout' and 'kdf' and compare 'plaintext'; for 'deterministic', rebuild the blob from eph_priv and nonce and compare it byte for byte; every 'negative' case must fail to open.

hello_frames.note: ts is fixed here for determinism. A live relay additionally requires |now - ts| <= 600 s, so to test against a running relay substitute the current time and re-sign. The relay trims and lowercases 'id' before every check; 'ts' must be a JSON integer.
relay_checks_in_order: id (trimmed, lowercased) is a valid fingerprint, else bad_field
pubkey and sig present, nonce length 16..64, else not_authorised
pubkey decodes to 32 bytes and sig decodes, else not_authorised
Ed25519 verify(pubkey, client_auth_string(id, ts, nonce), sig), else not_authorised

hello_signing_string.relay_hello_frame_fields: t=hello role=relay proto=1 node_id advertise ed25519(b64 pub) x25519(b64 pub) tls ws_port wss_port ts nonce version sig; the receiving relay checks nonce length 16..64, |now-ts| <= window, node_id == node_id_from_ed_pub(ed25519) and the signature over this string

signing.verify: Build each 'string' from its 'inputs' byte for byte (JSON-escaped here; '\n' is 0x0a, no trailing newline), sign it with RFC 8032 Ed25519 under 'signer' seed and compare 'sig_b64' exactly (Ed25519 is deterministic); verify each hello frame as the relay would and compare 'expected'.

x_r2r_auth_header.note: base64(compact JSON of the same proof object); decoded JSON <= 4096 bytes

storage_voucher.doc: White paper §14.4 and A.13. Keccak-256 uses the original Keccak padding (0x01), not SHA3-256 (0x06). The relay rebuilds the digest from its own vault address, chain id and payout address, recovers the secp256k1 signer (v in {27,28} or {0,1}; s must be <= n/2; the recovered address must be non-zero) and requires it to equal the rental's payment key.
notes: inner = keccak256("r2r-voucher-v1" || vault[20] || uint256_be(chain_id) || payee[20] || uint256_be(cumulative))
sig = r[32] || s[32] || v[1] as 0x + 130 hex; the relay lowercases it before decoding
address = 0x + hex(keccak256(X[32] || Y[32])[12..32]) of the uncompressed public key
